countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

aliases: Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science
Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering

courses.summary: A four-year undergraduate engineering degree in computer science and engineering, entered after twelve years of schooling with physics, chemistry and mathematics. Teaching combines programming, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, databases, computer networks and software engineering with laboratory work, and Indian universities commonly add a final-year project and an industry internship. Graduates enter software engineering, data and infrastructure roles or continue to a master's degree.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Civil Engineering
courses.summary: A four-year undergraduate engineering degree covering structural analysis and design, geotechnical engineering, transportation engineering, water resources, environmental engineering, surveying and construction management. Programmes pair lecture teaching with materials, hydraulics and surveying laboratories, site visits and a final-year design project. Graduates work in construction, infrastructure, consultancy and public works, or continue to a master's specialisation.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering
courses.summary: A four-year undergraduate engineering degree covering engineering mechanics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, machine design, manufacturing processes and control systems. Teaching is built around workshop practice, thermal and materials laboratories, computer-aided design and a final-year project. Graduates move into manufacturing, automotive, energy, thermal and design roles, or continue to a master's specialisation such as thermal engineering or machine design.

courses.name: Master of Business Administration
courses.summary: A two-year postgraduate management degree open to graduates of any discipline. The first year covers core functions such as accounting, finance, marketing, operations, organisational behaviour, economics and business analytics; the second year adds electives and specialisation. Full-time Indian MBA programmes normally include a summer internship between the two years, and selection typically combines an entrance-test score with a group discussion, written test and personal interview.

courses.metaDescription: What a two-year full-time MBA covers, which entrance tests are accepted, how selection works and what tuition and internship structure to expect.

courses.name: Bachelor of Laws
courses.summary: In India the LLB is most often taken as a five-year integrated honours degree combining a bachelor's in arts, business administration or science with the law curriculum, entered directly after twelve years of schooling. The syllabus covers constitutional law, contract, torts, criminal law, property, corporate law, procedure and jurisprudence, with moot courts, legal aid clinics and internships. Programmes must be recognised by the Bar Council of India for graduates to seek enrolment as advocates in India.

courses.name: Master of Laws
courses.summary: A postgraduate law degree for holders of a recognised bachelor's degree in law. Indian LLM programmes are commonly one year long and allow specialisation in areas such as constitutional law, business and corporate law, international law, criminal law, intellectual property or taxation. Assessment blends taught coursework with a dissertation, and the degree is used for academic careers, research, policy work and specialist practice rather than as a route to first enrolment as an advocate.

courses.name: M.Sc. in Biological Sciences
courses.summary: A two-year postgraduate science degree covering molecular biology, genetics, microbiology, biochemistry, cell biology, bioprocess technology and bioinformatics, depending on the chosen stream such as biotechnology or applied microbiology. Laboratory work is central, and most programmes end with a supervised research dissertation. Graduates move into research laboratories, biotechnology and pharmaceutical industry roles, quality and diagnostics work, or a doctoral programme.

courses.summary: A two-year postgraduate degree in population health, normally open to graduates of medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, allied health, life sciences and several non-clinical disciplines. Teaching covers epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy and management, environmental and occupational health, health economics and health promotion, with field placements and a dissertation. Graduates work in public health programmes, health systems management, non-governmental organisations and research.

universities.name: KIIT Deemed to be University
universities.summary: KIIT Deemed to be University is a private, self-financed institution at Patia in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, recognised under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. Its co-located schools cover engineering and computing, management, law, sciences and biotechnology, design, media and health, and it runs a separate international admissions route with tuition published in US dollars.
universities.campusLifestyle: KIIT reports a 36 sq km academic township holding 30 co-located schools, more than 3,000 faculty and researchers and over 40,000 learners, including around 2,000 international students from 65 countries and 131 international faculty. Each school runs from its own campus with dedicated laboratories, library and conference halls, alongside a multi-storey central library, 18 sports complexes, 30 food courts and the Biju Patnaik Indoor Stadium. The Central Convention Centre auditorium seats 1,600, and international students can join the India Trek cultural programme and credit-based study abroad options.
universities.cityProfile: KIIT sits at Patia in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, at postcode 751024. The Airports Authority of India operates Biju Patnaik International Airport in the city, which is the usual arrival point for international students, and lists the Lingaraj Temple and the Odisha State Museum among nearby attractions. The Odisha Department of Tourism names Bhubaneswar among the state's major cities alongside Cuttack, Puri and Rourkela. Inside and around the campus township there is a police station, an in-house computerised post office, banks and ATMs, and KIIT runs buses and shuttle cars for students and staff. Across most of India the southwest monsoon runs from June to September, so an August arrival lands towards the end of the wet season.
universities.practicalExposure: KIIT runs Centres of Excellence with named industry partners, including an SAP Centre of Excellence, an IBM Centre of Excellence, a Siemens Lab, an Intel Design Lab, a Tech Mahindra Design Lab, an NI Centre of Excellence and the ISRO KIIT Satellite Centre. Several postgraduate engineering specialisations are co-branded with industry: M.Tech in Next Generation Wireless Technology with Ericsson, M.Tech in Automotive Electronics and Software with KPIT Technologies of Pune, and M.Tech tracks in AI and Data Science, Internet of Things and Cybersecurity with LTIMindtree and L and T EduTech. KIIT Technology Business Incubator, opened in 2008 with Department of Science and Technology and NSTEDB support and recognised as a Centre of Excellence in 2018, supports more than 235 ventures. Public health and biotechnology students sit on a campus that includes Kalinga Institute of Medical Sciences, the university's own super-speciality teaching hospital, and KIIT School of Law operates a Legal Aid Service Clinic and a moot court programme. KIIT reports that more than 757 companies recruited on campus in 2025 with more than 4,621 job offers made; because an Indian Student visa does not permit employment in India, these figures describe institutional recruiting activity rather than any work entitlement for an international student.
universities.hostelOverview: Boys and girls hostels are separate, and KIIT runs a dedicated international hostel for foreign students. Rooms are offered on single, double and triple-sharing bases with attached bathrooms, Wi-Fi and intranet access, and KIIT states that about 30 per cent of hostel rooms are air conditioned. Every hostel has an attached canteen, a 24-hour reading room and facilities for indoor and outdoor games. Hostel, mess and examination charges sit outside the published US dollar tuition table and are confirmed in the admission offer letter, so no accommodation price is published in advance of an offer.
universities.dietarySupport: Each hostel has an attached canteen serving Indian and Continental food, and KIIT states that the on-campus mess caters to diverse culinary preferences with multi-cuisine meals and dietary-specific options. Food courts across the township specialise in cuisines from different parts of the world. Banks, ATMs and an in-house computerised post office operate inside the campus, and grocery and restaurant options in Patia and central Bhubaneswar are reachable on the campus bus and shuttle service.
universities.safetyOverview: KIIT publishes a Safety SOP Manual (Version 1.0, 2026) and lists an Anti-Ragging Committee, an Internal Complaints Committee, an Equal Opportunity Cell and a Student Grievance Redressal Committee with an Ombudsperson. A police station, banks and ATMs operate in and around the campus township, and the university publishes a 24x7 student support line alongside a separate student helpline.
universities.studentSupport: The International Relations Office is the first point of contact for student visa documentation, FRRO registration, visa extension, opening an Indian bank account and certificate authentication. A Dean Academics for International Students and a Faculty-in-Charge in every school handle academic queries, counselling is provided by a staff counsellor and a professional psychiatrist, and KIMS gives enrolled students free medical consultancy.

faq.question: Is KIIT a public or a private university?
faq.answer: KIIT is a private, self-financed institution. It holds Deemed to be University status under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, which is a Government of India recognition granting degree-awarding powers; it appears in the Odisha section of the UGC consolidated list of deemed universities and on the UGC list of deemed universities included under Section 12(B) of the UGC Act, and NAAC records it as accredited at grade A++ with a CGPA of 3.52 in Cycle 3.

faq.question: What is the language of instruction?
faq.answer: Programmes on the international route are taught in English throughout, with no transition to an Indian language part-way through the degree. KIIT additionally runs foundational English courses for non-native speakers, language workshops and sessions introducing basic Hindi for day-to-day communication outside the classroom.

faq.question: Who is eligible to apply through the KIIT international route?
faq.answer: The published international fee table is scoped to Foreign National applicants, including NRI, OCI and PIO applicants. Applicants from SAARC countries are placed on a separate, lower tuition tier. Applicants who do not fall into one of these categories are outside this route and would apply through the domestic KIITEE process instead.

faq.question: What does a year at KIIT cost for an international applicant?
faq.answer: KIIT publishes USD 10,000 a year for undergraduate courses, USD 10,000 a year for postgraduate courses, USD 4,000 a year for PhD, and USD 8,000 a year for undergraduate and postgraduate applicants from the SAARC region. Hostel, mess and examination charges are quoted separately and are confirmed in the admission offer letter, so a total annual budget can only be assembled once the offer is issued.

faq.question: How do I apply, and is there an application fee?
faq.answer: Applications go through the KIIT international admissions portal at international.kiit.ac.in. You register, verify your email from the message sent by kiit.global@kiit.ac.in, complete the programme, personal, address and educational-qualification sections, upload documents and submit. KIIT states that the international application is free of charge for foreign nationals and NRI candidates. The MBA at KIIT School of Management is the exception: foreign and NRI MBA applicants pay a US $50 application fee.

faq.question: Do I need IELTS or TOEFL?
faq.answer: KIIT lists proof of English proficiency such as TOEFL or IELTS among the upload items but marks it as not compulsory. Where documents were not issued in English, English translations are required. KIIT also conducts an online interview during the admission process to check eligibility, subject grasp and English knowledge, so English is assessed directly even without a test score.

faq.question: Is there an entrance exam for international applicants?
faq.answer: For most programmes the international route replaces the KIITEE entrance test with academic-record assessment plus an online interview. The MBA works differently: KIIT School of Management assesses foreign and NRI candidates on a valid GMAT score taken in 2025 for 2026 admission, followed by a Group Discussion, Personal Interview and Writing Ability Test.

faq.question: Can I study medicine or architecture through this route?
faq.answer: No. The KIIT international fee page states that admission to medical courses other than allied medical courses is on the basis of a NEET score only, and that Bachelor of Architecture is on the basis of a NATA score only. NEET is administered by the National Testing Agency and foreign, NRI and OCI candidates are eligible to sit it, but eligibility for a particular seat still depends on state and institution rules. Allied and non-clinical health programmes such as the Master of Public Health are outside that restriction.

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when should I apply?
faq.answer: KIIT academic calendars show an Autumn Academic Session opening on 22 August with reporting, registration and induction on the first two days, and a Spring Academic Session opening on 2 January. The KIIT International Relations Office states that the international application window for each academic year runs from 1 March to 30 September.

faq.question: Can I work part-time while studying at KIIT?
faq.answer: No. The Bureau of Immigration states that a holder of an Indian Student visa is not permitted to undertake employment or business activity in India. This applies for the whole duration of the course, so no part-time earnings should be built into a funding plan for study in India. Any budget needs to be covered by savings, family support or scholarship.

faq.question: What scholarships are available to international students?
faq.answer: KIIT states that its International Scholarship Programme awards 100 per cent or 50 per cent of the total fee on merit, covering tuition, books, air-conditioned accommodation, multi-cuisine mess, 24/7 library and internet access, laptop, registration and examination fees, with MBBS, dental, nursing and architecture courses excluded. Separately, government routes such as the Indian Council for Cultural Relations schemes and Study in India scholarships are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions or the national portal, not through the university. Award numbers are not published, so no scholarship should be assumed when budgeting.

faq.question: What accreditation does KIIT hold, and what does it mean for me?
faq.answer: KIIT is a Deemed to be University under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, is on the UGC Section 12(B) list, and holds NAAC accreditation at grade A++, CGPA 3.52, Cycle 3, declared August 2022. The NBA register shows current Tier I accreditation under the Washington Accord for five B.Tech branches - civil, computer science, electrical, mechanical, and electronics and telecommunication - to 30 June 2028; other programmes are not covered by it. The Bar Council of India approved-CLE list records KIIT School of Law with approval to 2026-27. Whether an Indian degree is recognised in your home country is decided by that country's own regulator.

faq.question: What does registration after arrival involve?
faq.answer: A Student visa valid for more than 180 days requires registration with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO after arrival; the deadline depends on nationality, and Nepalese and Bhutanese citizens are exempt from visa and registration requirements. The Bureau of Immigration also requires a Non-Resident Ordinary bank account with a recognised Indian bank, with details given to the FRRO. The KIIT International Relations Office handles FRRO registration, visa extension, bank-account opening and certificate authentication as part of its arrival support.
